newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Attack on Serbs followed disappearance of Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Attack on Serbs followed disappearance of Moslems.

text.p: A shooting attack on a Bosnian Serb civilian car from the edge of Bosnian government territory may have been a reprisal for the reported disappearance of a few Moslem security police in the area, Western sources say.

"The ambush of the Serb car may have been an act of revenge because the Bosnians say around eight members of the Black Swans vanished in the vicinity recently," said an official familiar with human-rights monitoring in postwar Bosnia.

The Black Swans are an elite paramilitary police unit which, among other things, comprises the presidential security detail in the mostly Moslem Bosnian government and also fought on several fronts in the 1992-95 war.
Serbs who carved out a breakaway state in the war allege that Black Swans committed atrocities against Serb civilians.

Violence along postwar Bosnia's so-called Inter-Entity Boundary Line (IEBL), which divides the Serb republic from the Moslem-Croat federation, has surged in the approach to countrywide general elections on September 14.

On Friday up to 10 gunmen in civilian clothes fired on a Serb car in an ambush on a road south of Sarajevo that crosses alternating patches of separatist Serb and Bosnian government territory, a NATO peace force spokesman said.
A 60-year-old woman riding with two children in the back seat of the car was hit by four bullets and later hospitalised with a collapsed lung and other injuries.
The car was forced to stop and two Serb men in the front seats were dragged out by the civilian assailants.
NATO Lieutenant Colonel Max Marriner said the Serbs were bundled into a white four-wheel drive car which sped off towards the government-controlled village of Pendici.
U.N. police monitors originally said on Friday that the two Serb men, one of whom was believed to have been shot as well, were detained by Bosnian government police.
But Ivanko said the Serbs actually went missing and Bosnian police were looking for them.
"We have observed an increase in Serb republic police presence near the IEBL since the shooting but no increase in tension is evident," he told Reuters.
